published_prior_art.cite: LiZhao2026AdaptiveDesignBased supplies adaptive block-AIPW martingale theory; GaoGeQian2025MOT supplies static MOT identified sets, but neither gives a predictable adaptive transport envelope.
LiZhao2026AdaptiveDesignBased supplies the general block-adaptive martingale reduction; the explicit two-block enumeration is an implementation diagnostic.
AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance supplies two-arm rearrangement; GaoGeQian2025MOT supplies finite multi-marginal OT computation.
AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance contains the underlying two-arm rearrangement extremality; this is a useful explicit adaptive-formula test witness.
YuZhuLiu2025SharpStratified treats nonadaptive stratified empirical endpoints and OberReynolds2023OTFunctionals treats static OT endpoint estimation, not history-uniform predictable arrays.

Saco2026SelfNormalizedAdaptiveExperiments gives superpopulation realized-QV studentization, while LiZhao2026AdaptiveDesignBased gives conservative adaptive design-based inference without this transport upper endpoint.
AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance, MikhaeilGreen2024RegressionSharpVariance, and YuZhuLiu2025SharpStratified are intentionally recovered special cases.
AronowGreenLee2014SharpVariance establishes static completion sharpness and GaoGeQian2025MOT permits fractional MOT plans; neither resolves ex-ante attainment along endogenous adaptive histories.

soundness_flags.label: Open-ended Question 8 / def:completion-class
soundness_flags.one_line: Because the residual margins μ_nba depend on past-fitted, history-random g_nbi(a), membership of an ex-ante deterministic potential-outcome completion in C_n is not defined before randomization; replace C_n with an explicitly history-tree-indexed or rectangular completion class.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract; Section 5, “Extension to block adaptive designs”
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper gives finite-population IPW/AIPW theory under general adaptive designs and an adaptive-regression covariance estimator that is sharp under residual additivity; its block extension permits prior outcomes to affect later-block allocation.

The proceedings paper casts causal partial identification with K margins as MOT, obtains the exact identified set, and gives plug-in results for quadratic objectives; it is static rather than an adaptive-design result.
The paper gives consistent sharp variance bounds for a difference-in-means estimator under complete randomization and uses its upper bound for asymptotically narrowest conservative Wald intervals.

source_verification_receipts.version: arXiv v2, 26 June 2024; published Statistics in Medicine version is paywalled
source_verification_receipts.locator: Abstract and Introduction, especially pp. 1-2 equivalent HTML lines 51-65
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The accessible theorem text concerns fixed-potential-outcome stratified complete randomization, sharp weighted difference-in-means variance estimation, and growing-strata empirical-process control; it does not analyze outcome-adaptive future counts.
The paper extends Aronow--Green--Lee sharp bounds to general regression adjustment in nonadaptive randomized experiments.
The paper characterizes sharp OT endpoint identified sets and gives root-n plug-in and bootstrap inference for static joint-potential-outcome functionals.

The paper assumes i.i.d. arrivals, logged propensities, and predictable nuisance fitting, proves a martingale score representation, and studentizes by realized quadratic variation without deterministic variance stabilization.
The paper characterizes admissible conservative quadratic variance bounds under interference and complex designs; its criterion is not marginal-coupling sharpness.
The four-arm trial ran over 12 minitrials and used a participant-level contextual multi-armed bandit after the first minitrial, explicitly with no minimum or maximum allocation to trial arms.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a rectangular, history-tree-indexed completion object: fix potential outcomes ex ante, specify how each possible pre-block history induces g and residual margins, and phrase completion sharpness over that object rather than the currently path-dependent C_n.

Add an explicit two-block worked instance showing a single fixed completion, its two possible histories, and the resulting nodewise transport values; this will distinguish local convexified sharpness from ex-ante sharpness transparently.

Strengthen the empirical contribution with a stated fixed-K computational bound or a rate for the transport program over the adaptive history, and benchmark its interval width against Li--Zhao’s conservative covariance estimator.

recommended_next_step: Revise the completion class and Open-ended Question 8 into a history-tree-defined ex-ante completion problem, then advance the otherwise field-tier kernel to Stage 0.
